structure.title: Preface
structure.summary:
# Description of Partial Document

This is a Hardware Guide for the HUAWEI NetEngine 8000 X Series (versions V800R012C10 to V800R023C00), Issue 06 dated June 30, 2026. The document covers the following main points:

## Key Content Areas:

1. **Document Information & Legal Notice** - Copyright, trademark information, and usage disclaimers from Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.

2. **Hardware Tool Usage** - Instructions on using hardware tools for the NetEngine 8000 X Series.

3. **Hardware Description** - Comprehensive technical specifications including:
   - **Chassis Models**: Detailed descriptions of three variants:
     - NetEngine 8000 X4
     - NetEngine 8000 X8
     - NetEngine 8000 X16
   
   - **Power Supply Systems**: Multiple power supply configurations for each device model, including:
     - AC and High-Voltage DC Power Modules (PAH-3000WA)
     - DC Power Supplies (PDC-2200WC, PDC-3000WA, PDC-4000WA)
     - Power Switch specifications
   
   - **Heat Dissipation/Cooling Systems**: 
     - Overview of heat dissipation architecture
     - Chassis door specifications for X4 and X8 devices
     - Multiple fan tray assemblies (FAN-240SB-B, FAN-480SB-B, FAN-480SE-B, FAN-960SB-B)

4. **Info-Finder Tool** - Reference for locating specific hardware information.

nodes.summary:
# Document Description

This is a hardware guide for the Huawei NetEngine 8000 X Series networking equipment. The main points covered include:

1. **Document Declaration and Hardware Tool Usage** - Introduction and basic tool information

2. **Hardware Description** - Comprehensive technical specifications covering:
   - **Chassis Models** - Three variants: NetEngine 8000 X4, X8, and X16 with detailed specifications for each
   - **Power Supply Systems** - Multiple power supply configurations for each chassis model, including:
     - AC and High-Voltage DC Power Modules (PAH-3000WA)
     - DC Power Supplies (PDC series with varying wattages: 2200W, 3000W, 4000W)
     - Power switches for managing multiple power inputs
   - **Heat Dissipation and Cooling Systems** - Including:
     - Chassis door specifications for X4 and X8 models
     - Multiple fan tray assemblies (FAN-240SB-B, FAN-480SB-B, FAN-480SE-B, FAN-960SB-B) with varying cooling capacities

The document serves as a technical reference guide providing detailed hardware specifications, component descriptions, and system configurations for the NetEngine 8000 X Series equipment line.

# Description of Partial Document

4. **Optical modules section**: Introduction to pluggable optical modules documentation.

# Main Points Covered in the Partial Document

This section of the HUAWEI NetEngine 8000 X Series Hardware Guide provides detailed specifications and documentation for:

1. **Integrated Line Processing Units (LPUI)** - Multiple variants of 8-port 400GBase-QSFP-DD and 8-port 100GBase-QSFP28 processing units with different configurations (LPUI-4T variants), including models with different default 100GE enablement options (8*100GE or 16*100GE)

2. **High-Capacity Processing Units** - LPUI-7.2T and LPUI-14.4T units supporting 18-port and 36-port 400GBase-QSFP-DD configurations respectively

3. **Flexible Cards** - P1T and P2T flexible card series supporting various port configurations including 100GBase-QSFP28, 10GBase LAN/WAN-SFP+, and 400GBase-QSFP-DD with FlexE and MACsec capabilities

4. **Optical Modules and Components** - Comprehensive coverage of pluggable optical modules including:
   - Optical module structure, classification, and usage guidelines
   - Optical amplifiers and their applications
   - Various eSFP optical modules at different speeds (155Mbps, 1.25Gbps) with different wavelengths and transmission distances
   - BIDI (bidirectional) and CWDM (Coarse Wavelength Division Multiplexing) optical modules
   - Electrical modules for 1Gbps connections

nodes.title: Optical Module Structure
nodes.summary:
# Description of Partial Document

This section of a technical hardware guide covers optical and electrical modules for the Huawei NetEngine 8000 X Series. The main points include:

1. **Optical Module Fundamentals** - Structure, classification, appearance, usage instructions, interoperation rules, and attenuator configuration

2. **Optical Amplifier Overview** - Functions, physical characteristics, usage scenarios, and operational guidelines

3. **155Mbps eSFP Optical Modules** - Multiple variants with different wavelengths (1550nm, 1310nm) and transmission distances (15km-80km)

4. **155Mbps eSFP BIDI Optical Modules** - Bidirectional modules with dual wavelengths for simultaneous transmission and reception

5. **1Gbps Electrical Module** - Standard electrical connectivity option

6. **1.25Gbps eSFP Optical Modules** - Multiple configurations supporting both multimode fiber (MMF) and single-mode fiber (SMF) with various wavelengths and distances

7. **1.25Gbps eSFP BIDI Optical Modules** - Bidirectional variants with multiple wavelength combinations and transmission distances (10km-80km)

8. **1.25Gbps eSFP CWDM Optical Modules** - Coarse wavelength division multiplexing modules at different wavelengths (1511nm-1591nm) for 80km transmission

Each module type includes detailed specifications, model numbers, and page references for comprehensive technical documentation.

This section of the HUAWEI NetEngine 8000 X Series Hardware Guide provides comprehensive documentation on optical and electrical modules. The main points covered include:

## General Optical Module Information
- Optical module structure, classification, and physical appearance
- Usage instructions and interoperation rules
- Optical attenuator configuration
- Optical amplifier overview, functions, appearance, usage scenarios, and operational guidance

**155Mbps Modules:**
- Standard eSFP optical modules with various wavelengths (1550nm, 1310nm) and transmission distances (15-80km)
- Bidirectional (BIDI) eSFP modules with different transmit/receive wavelength combinations

**1Gbps Modules:**
- Electrical SFP modules for shorter distances (100m)

**1.25Gbps Modules:**
- Standard eSFP optical modules supporting multimode fiber (MMF) and single-mode fiber (SMF) with various wavelengths and distances
- Bidirectional (BIDI) eSFP modules with multiple wavelength and distance configurations
- Coarse Wavelength Division Multiplexing (CWDM) modules with 8 different wavelength options
- Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (DWDM) modules with 37 different wavelength channels supporting 120km transmission distances

All modules are documented with specific technical specifications, model numbers, and page references for detailed information.

nodes.title: Introduction to the Power Distribution System
nodes.summary:
# Description of Partial Document

This section of a technical hardware guide covers the installation and configuration procedures for the HUAWEI NetEngine 8000 X Series equipment. The main points include:

1. **Power Distribution System Introduction** - Overview of the power distribution infrastructure for the devices

2. **Device Connection Methods** - Detailed instructions for connecting three device types (X4, X8, and X16) to Power Distribution Frames (PDFs) using multiple power configurations:
   - Direct AC connections
   - Direct DC connections
   - High-Voltage DC connections
   - Three-Phase PDU connections
   - High-Voltage DC PDU connections

3. **Device Unpacking Procedures** - Instructions for unpacking both cartons and individual cards

4. **Chassis Installation** - Step-by-step guidance for installing X4, X8, and X16 devices, including optional bracket adjustments

5. **Additional Module Installation** - Comprehensive instructions for installing various system components including:
   - Filler panels and cable management frames
   - Power modules and enclosures
   - Fan modules, SFUs, and trays
   - MPUs, LPUs, and flexible cards
   - Optical modules and optional accessories (chassis doors, noise reduction modules)

6. **PDU Cabinet Installation** - Procedures for installing Power Distribution Units into cabinets

structure.title: Document Declaration
structure.summary:
# Main Points of the Document

This is the Document Declaration section of the HUAWEI NetEngine 8000 X Series Hardware Guide. The main points covered include:

1. **Purpose**: Provides detailed hardware information about the NetEngine 8000 X, including chassis, boards, and cables, with installation and maintenance instructions.

2. **Applicable Product Versions**: Lists seven supported software versions (V800R012C10SPC300 through V800R023C00SPC500) that the document covers.

3. **Intended Audience**: Targets network planning engineers, hardware installation engineers, commissioning engineers, on-site maintenance engineers, and system maintenance engineers.

4. **Special Declarations**: Notes that hardware pictures are for reference only, supported boards are subject to pre-sales information, and device dimensions are design specifications without manufacturing tolerances.

5. **Symbol Conventions**: Defines safety and informational symbols used throughout the document, including hazard levels (high, medium, low risk), equipment damage warnings, and notice/note indicators.

6. **Change History**: Documents six official releases from Issue 01 (2024-06-30) through Issue 06 (2026-06-30).

structure.title: Using the Hardware Tool
structure.summary:
# Description of Partial Document

This section describes the Info-Finder tool platform used in enterprise networks for accessing product information. The main points covered include:

1. **Purpose of Info-Finder**: A searchable tool platform for locating key product information organized by product series and model

2. **Types of Information Available**:
   - Basic information (software specifications, life cycles, hardware information)
   - Operation and maintenance information (licenses, alarms, logs, commands, MIBs)

3. **Hardware-Related Tools Provided**:
   - **Product Image Gallery**: Offers product photos and network element icons for creating design drawings and networking diagrams
   - **Hardware Configuration**: Automatically generates hardware configuration diagrams and calculates weight, power consumption, and heat consumption based on selected components
   - **Hardware Center**: Provides technical specifications of devices and components, plus device-component-version mapping
   - **3D Model Function**: Enables querying of product images, product overviews, and component insertion/removal videos for quick one-stop product information access

nodes.title: X8 device Power Supply System
nodes.summary:
# Main Points Covered in the Partial Document

## Input Requirements for DC Power Supply
- Support for -48 V DC input in DC power distribution scenarios
- Protection component requirements based on power module wattage (63 A for 2200 W, 82 A for 3000 W, 113 A for 4000 W)
- Derating requirements for protection components like fuses and circuit breakers
- Input circuit breakers must match output circuit breakers on customer PDF side

## X8 Device Power Supply System Overview
- Supports DC, AC, and HVDC power supplies
- Connects to external power distribution through Power Entry Module (PEM)
- Supports dual power sources (A and B) with N+1 redundancy capability
- Each Power Module (PM) has two inputs for power conversion

## Power Source Configuration Guidelines
- Single power source: connect to all A or all B sockets
- Dual power sources in AC/HVDC: default to source A with automatic failover to B
- Load-balancing mode: distribute sources across A and B sockets
- DC scenarios: connect sources to separate A and B socket groups
- Automatic switching between 220V AC and HVDC inputs when both available

## Power Supply System Components
- Power Modules (PMs): convert and distribute power
- Power Switches: control PM output with mutual backup
- Power Entry Module (PEM): connects to external power distribution with areas A and B

## PM and PEM Applications
- Multiple power supply scenarios with different PEM/PM combinations
- DC PEMs support 2200W, 3000W, and 4000W DC PMs
- AC & HVDC PEMs support 3000W dual-input AC & HVDC PMs
- Flexible configuration based on overall power consumption

## Power Supply Architecture
- DC power supply: 20 inputs (10 per source) with dual-input PMs
- AC & HVDC power supply: 20 inputs with support for PDU connections
- Three modes: AC only, HVDC only, or AC & HVDC hybrid
- Power sources A and B provide mutual backup

## AC & HVDC PEM Details
- Pre-installed and cannot be removed, installed, or replaced onsite
- Integrated into chassis with no onsite configuration needed

This document section covers the specifications and heat dissipation system of the NetEngine 8000 series devices:

## Item Specifications
- Maximum input current: 113 A
- Rated output voltage: 53.5 V
- Rated output current: 75 A
- Rated output power: 4000 W
- Power supply efficiency: 0.96
- Power dissipation mode: Built-in fan

## Heat Dissipation System Overview
- The system comprises fan modules and an optional chassis door
- Fan modules are installed at the rear to cool MPUs, LPUs, and SFUs using front-to-back airflow
- Power modules have dedicated fans to manage their heat generation and maintain normal operating temperatures
- The optional chassis door shields electromagnetic noise and prevents dust ingress

## Heat Dissipation Process for Cards
- MPUs and LPUs feature front panels with air holes for cold air intake
- Cool air flows through MPUs and LPUs toward SFUs
- Hot air is exhausted from the chassis by rear fan modules
- Vacant power module and card slots must be covered with filler panels to ensure efficient heat dissipation and EMC compliance

nodes.title: Overview of the Heat Dissipation System
nodes.summary:
# Main Points of the Partial Document

## Item Specifications
- Maximum input current: 113 A
- Rated output voltage: 53.5 V
- Rated output current: 75 A
- Rated output power: 4000 W
- Power supply efficiency: 0.96
- Power dissipation mode: Built-in fan

## Heat Dissipation System Overview
The document describes the heat dissipation system for NetEngine 8000 series devices, which consists of:
- Fan modules at the rear of the device
- Optional chassis door at the front

## Heat Dissipation of Cards (MPUs, LPUs, and SFUs)
- Uses front-to-back airflow design
- Cold air enters through front panel air holes
- Cool air flows through cards to SFUs
- Hot air is exhausted from the chassis by fan modules
- Vacant card slots must be covered with filler panels for efficient heat dissipation and EMC compliance

## Heat Dissipation of Power Modules
- Uses front-to-back airflow design
- Cold air enters through power module panel air holes
- Built-in fans blow air through the power module area
- Hot air passes through the power backplane and exits through holes on the PEM (Power Entry Module)

## Hardware Identification and Numbering
- **Subcard ID**: Identifies slot locations for subcards on NetEngine 8000 series devices, with fixed cards having ID 0 and FPICs starting from 0

- **Port Rate Description**: Nominal data transmission rates supported by pluggable modules including 400GE, 100GE, 50GE, 40GE, 25GE, 10GE, and GE

- **Port Auto-Negotiation**: Enables connected ports to exchange information and automatically configure transmission capabilities including duplex mode, rate, and FEC
- **Port Split**: Allows high-bandwidth physical ports to be split into multiple independent lower-bandwidth ports for flexible networking and cost reduction
- **Port Rate Configuration**: Ability to change interface rates through port split dimension commands

- **Benefits**: Reduces initial costs, lowers purchase threshold, allows step-by-step capacity expansion, and enables flexible investment based on service requirements

- Port rate is determined by pluggable modules and can be affected by various factors
- **Port Rate Auto-Sensing**: Allows ports to automatically work at the rate of installed media without manual commands

- **Port Split**: Allows high-bandwidth ports to be split into multiple lower-bandwidth ports for flexible networking and cost reduction
- **Port Rate Configuration**: Manual configuration option using port split dimension commands

## Consumption Model (CM)
- A flexible hardware sales model enabling customers to purchase large-capacity boards in installments
- Reduces initial costs and allows step-by-step capacity expansion through hardware licenses
- **Key Components**: CM-supporting hardware boards, Hardware Right to Use (RTU) licenses (mandatory), and Service licenses (optional)
- **Comparison with Conventional Model**: CM offers on-demand flexible purchase versus conventional model's all-at-once board capacity
- **Application Procedure**: Six-step process from purchasing boards to configuring services
- **Benefits**: Reduced initial investment, improved slot utilization (2-4 fold improvement), and reduced operational expenses through remote license loading

This document excerpt from the HUAWEI NetEngine 8000 X Series Hardware Guide provides detailed technical specifications for three variants of enhanced Small Form-factor Pluggable (eSFP) optical transceiver modules designed for long-distance telecommunications. The main points covered include:

## Module Overview
- Three similar eSFP modules with different center wavelengths (1554.13 nm, 1553.33 nm, and 1552.52 nm)
- All designed for 120 km transmission distance over single-mode fiber (SMF)
- Commercial-grade modules with specific part numbers and model designations

## Key Technical Specifications
- **Transmission Rate**: 155 Mbit/s to 2.67 Gbit/s
- **Operating Temperature**: 0°C to 70°C
- **Power Consumption**: Maximum 1.3 W
- **Bit Error Ratio**: <1x10E-12
- **Connector Type**: LC connectors
- **ESD Protection**: 500 V (HBM1)

## Optical Characteristics
- **Transmitter**: Center wavelengths around 1552-1554 nm, maximum optical power of 4 dBm, minimum extinction ratio of 8.2 dB
- **Receiver**: Operating wavelength range 1520-1570 nm, sensitivity of -28 dBm, overload power of -8 dBm

## Standards and Compliance
- Application standards: SONET OC-48 LR-2, Gigabit Ethernet
- Environmental: RoHS compliant
- Security: FCC Class B, IEC 60825-1 Class 1
- DDM options: SFF-8472

- Attenuators are required for pigtail loopback and short-distance interconnection scenarios

## Interconnection Requirements
- Optical power measurement must be performed before connecting two optical modules
- WDM device client-side 1+1 protection switching time exceeds 50 ms
- 40 km transmission requires Huawei optical modules with identical part numbers
- Link insertion loss must be less than 17 dB when used with 02312AXF modules

- Distributes four AC three-phase 32A (MAX) inputs into twenty-four 16A (MAX) outputs

- Requires 3# screwdriver and flat-head screwdriver (0.6mm x 3.5mm) for installation

nodes.title: Installing a DC PDB (02122145)
nodes.summary:
# Main Points Covered in the Partial Document

## DC Power Distribution Box (PDB) Installation Guide

**Safety Requirements and Tools:**
- Ground cable must be securely connected to PDB using M6 screws with 5 N·m torque
- Required tools: #3 screwdriver for input/ground cables and 0.6 mm x 3.5 mm flat-head screwdriver for output cables
- PDB uses 32 A circuit breakers derated to 16 A
- Power must be disconnected before connecting cables

**Installation Procedure for DC PDB (Model 02122145):**
1. Remove temporary protective cover from the PDB
2. Install guide rails 4 U below cabinet top, aligned with mounting rail scale lines
3. Install floating nuts in specific positions (3rd and 10th holes) on mounting bars
4. Push PDB into cabinet along guide rails and secure with four screws (requires 2-3 persons)
5. Connect ground cable to equipment room grounding copper bar (not to cabinet ground point)

**Important Compatibility and Technical Notes:**
- Guide rails may be incompatible with third-party cabinets
- Ground cable requirements: 35 mm²/50 mm² for 125 A/250 A single input current (cabinet's 16 mm² cable is insufficient)
- Do not step on air filter during installation
- Use cables of appropriate length with terminals already attached

# Main Points of Section 4.9 Line Planning

This section covers power cable routing planning for the X4 device, specifically addressing AC and High-Voltage DC power cable connections. The key points include:

1. **Pre-planning Requirement**: Advance planning of power cable routing is necessary to ensure proper connection order.

2. **Single Power Source Scenario**: When only one power source is available, all power modules should connect to either power source A or B terminals/sockets.

3. **Dual Power Source Scenarios**:
   - In AC or high-voltage DC: Power source A is default with automatic failover to B if A fails
   - In DC scenarios: Higher voltage source provides higher current when voltages differ
   - With mixed AC & high-voltage DC inputs: 220V AC is default with automatic switchover to high-voltage DC if AC fails

4. **Power Distribution Requirements**: Output power from both sources A and B must exceed the device's maximum input power.

5. **Cabling Infrastructure Support**: The cabinet supports both overhead and underfloor cabling options, with third-party cabinet cabling requiring separate evaluation.

**Cable Types:**

nodes.summary:
# Equipment Room Setup and Environmental Requirements

## Main Points Covered:

1. **Environmental Precautions**
   - Avoid placing air conditioning vents to blow directly on equipment to prevent condensation
   - Do not use sulfur-containing decorative materials in the equipment room

2. **Equipment Room Layout Principles**
   - Separate different types of equipment (mobile switching, telecommunications, power supply, auxiliary) into different rooms
   - Minimize cabling distance for easier maintenance and reduced faults
   - Bundle and route different cable types (AC power, DC power, RF, ground, transmission, control) separately and neatly
   - Maintain minimum 30 mm separation between ground cables and other cable types

3. **Construction Requirements**
   - Minimum room height: 3 meters
   - Floor specifications: semi-conductive, dustproof, preferably raised floor with ESD covering with specific tolerance standards
   - Floor load-bearing capacity must accommodate equipment weight
   - Door dimensions: 2 m high × 1 m wide with dustproof sealing
   - Windows: double-pane glass, tightly sealed

# Main Points of AC Power Supply Requirements and Recommendations

## Voltage and Frequency Standards
- AC power supply voltage tolerance ranges: -10% to +5% for devices, and -15% to +10% for power modules and important buildings
- Alternating current frequency tolerance: -4% to +4% of rated value
- Voltage waveform must be sinusoidal with distortion within 5% of rated voltage

- Automated electric generators must support standard interfaces with telecommunication protocols, remote monitoring, and control capabilities
- AC neutral conductors must match the cross-sectional area of phase lines
- AC cables must have non-flammable insulation and comply with local regulations

- Voltage regulating or stabilizing devices are required when mains voltage exceeds device tolerance ranges

- Storage batteries should typically be installed in parallel configuration (two groups), with UPS batteries in single group configuration
- Redundancy for UPS systems can be achieved through concatenation or parallel connection
- Active and backup inverters should be determined based on maximum power requirements

nodes.summary:
# Main Points of DC Power Supply Requirements and Recommendations

## Requirements for DC Power Supply (Section 4.18.2.3)

1. **General Requirements**: Equipment rooms need stable and reliable DC power with power equipment deployed close to telecommunications equipment to minimize feeder length and reduce voltage drop (less than 3.2V from battery to equipment port).

2. **Deployment by Enterprise Scale**:
   - Large-scale enterprises: Independent power supply system per floor
   - Medium-scale enterprises: Centralized power supply (power and battery rooms) or distributed systems
   - Small-scale enterprises: Integrated system in equipment room with corrosive gas prevention measures

3. **Technical Specifications** (Table 4-66):
   - DC power capacity must exceed 1.5 times rated current for surge support
   - Regulated voltage precision: ≤1% (output range -46.0V to -56.4V under specified AC input and load conditions)
   - Switch on/off overshoot: ±5% of integral DC output voltage
   - Peak noise voltage: ≤200 mV
   - Dynamic response: Recovery time <200 ms with ±5% overshoot range

## Recommendations for DC Power Supply (Section 4.18.2.4)

1. Use distributed power supply mode with multiple systems in multiple locations
2. Adopt standard DC power supply systems with output voltage within required range
3. Improve AC power supply reliability to reduce battery storage capacity requirements

   - Correct directional feeding to ensure proper text positioning

   - All content must be on the label, not on backing layer

nodes.summary:
# Description of Partial Document

This section of the HUAWEI NetEngine 8000 X Series Hardware Guide provides a comprehensive guide to using optical modules, covering common faults, prevention measures, and precautions.

## Main Points Covered:

**Common Faults of Optical Modules:**
- Incomplete installation of optical modules and unsecured latch bosses
- Contamination of optical receptacles leading to reduced coupling efficiency and signal loss
- Burnt optical modules caused by excessive optical power without proper attenuation

**Prevention Measures:**

1. **Preventing Loosened Optical Modules:**
   - Proper insertion technique with audible/tactile confirmation (click or shake)
   - Correct positioning of release handles
   - Verification of secure installation through pull-out testing

2. **Preventing Receptacle Contamination:**
   - Cleaning optical connectors before insertion using special cleaning tissues
   - Using protective caps on unused modules and connectors
   - Proper fiber management and storage
   - Cleaning procedures for long-unused receptacles and connectors
   - Troubleshooting signal loss through cleaning

3. **Preventing Optical Module Burnout:**
   - Disconnecting optical fibers before OTDR testing
   - Using optical attenuators during self-loop tests

**General Precautions:**
- Vertical insertion of optical connectors
- Matching fiber types to corresponding optical module types (multimode/single mode)

The document also includes a Fault Tag template for documenting equipment issues and repairs.
